instruction:
Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL to build and solve a 3D transient thermal conduction model.

Physical problem:
One-dimensional transient heat conduction in a semi-infinite-like steel block.

Coordinate system and geometry:
- Use the global Cartesian coordinate system.
- Heat conduction is along the X direction.
- The long direction of the block is X.
- The block occupies:
  - 0 ≤ X ≤ 50 mm
  - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 20 mm
  - 0 ≤ Z ≤ 20 mm
- The left end face is the face at X = 0.
- The other end face is the face at X = 50 mm.
- The model should behave as a one-dimensional conduction problem along X.

Model parameters:
- Block size: 50 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm
- Material: steel
- Use a unit-consistent mm-s-J-kg-°C system:
  - Thermal conductivity: 0.05 W/(mm·°C), equivalent to 50 W/(m·K)
  - Specific heat: 460 J/(kg·°C)
  - Density: 7.85e-6 kg/mm³, equivalent to 7850 kg/m³
- Element type: SOLID70
- Mesh: global element size 2 mm
- The mesh should contain nodes at X = 4 mm and X = 6 mm. A regular 2 mm mesh along X satisfies this requirement.

Boundary and initial conditions:
- Initial temperature of the whole model: 20 °C
- Left end face at X = 0: prescribed temperature 100 °C
- All other external surfaces, including X = 50 mm, Y = 0, Y = 20 mm, Z = 0, and Z = 20 mm, are adiabatic.

Analysis type:
- Transient thermal analysis
- Total analysis time: 10 s
- Initial time step: 0.1 s
- Save the final result at t = 10 s.

Save requirements:
- Use C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop as the ANSYS working directory.
- Save the database file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\apdl_transient_thermal.db
- Save the thermal result file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\apdl_transient_thermal.rth
